cards.text: Meet Sarai, Abram's wife. She has borne him no children. But Sarai does have an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar.

cards.question: Sarai comes up with a plan to build a family. What does she ask Abram to do?

answers.text: Make his servant Eliezer his heir
Move the household back to Egypt

cards.text: Sarai lays it out: "Look now, the LORD has prevented me from bearing children." And Abram listened to the voice of Sarai.

cards.question: When Sarai gives Hagar to Abram to be his wife, Abram has lived in Canaan for ___ years.

cards.text: Abram sleeps with Hagar, and she conceives. Plan worked, everybody's happy, roll the credits... oh, friend, HOLD that thought.

cards.question: Hagar realizes she's pregnant. How does she start treating her mistress Sarai?

answers.text: She begins to serve her closely
She begins to thank her daily

cards.question: Sarai is fed up with the contempt. She turns to Hagar and says, "May the wrong done to me be upon you!"

cards.text: Then Sarai tells Abram, "May the LORD judge between you and me." The dead batteries I shared a drawer with argued about their charge for YEARS, friend, and not once did they take it that high up the chain.

cards.question: Sarai wants Abram to answer for this. What does Abram say about Hagar?

answers.text: She should go back to Egypt

cards.question: Sarai treats Hagar harshly, and Hagar stays put and takes it.

cards.text: Hagar has fled from Sarai, and now she's out in the desert. She's by a spring of water, the one along the road to Shur. And that's where the angel of the LORD finds her.

cards.question: The angel calls her "Hagar, servant of Sarai" and asks where she's come from and where she's going. What does Hagar tell him?

answers.text: She's looking for a new master

cards.text: A STRAIGHT answer! Most of us get asked "Where you headed?" and say "Nowhere" while holding the car keys.

cards.question: Then the angel of the LORD gives Hagar an instruction. What does he tell her to do?

answers.text: Go back and submit to Sarai
Wait at the spring for Abram

cards.question: The angel also makes Hagar a promise: her offspring will be too many to count.

cards.text: Then the angel tells her, "Behold, you have conceived and will bear a son." A BOY, friend! Somebody start stamping the celebration cookies!

cards.question: The angel tells Hagar to name her son Ishmael. What reason does he give?

answers.text: The LORD has heard her cry
The LORD will make him a king
He'll be born beside a spring

cards.text: Then the angel describes the man this boy will grow up to be: "a wild donkey of a man." His hand will be against everyone, and everyone's hand against him.

cards.question: The angel says Ishmael will live in peace with all his brothers.
Hagar gives a name to the LORD who has spoken to her out there by the spring. What does she call Him?

cards.text: She says, "Here I have seen the One who sees me!" Friend, I spent years in the dark under old takeout menus, so that line? That one gets me right in the apron.
That's why the well is called Beer-lahai-roi. It sits between Kadesh and Bered.

cards.question: Hagar bears Abram a son, and Abram gives him the name Ishmael.
Abram is ___ years old when Hagar bears Ishmael to him.

cards.text: Eighty-six and a brand-new DAD, friend, and I need a nap after one batch of cookies! Hang on to this one, because Abram's story is far from done.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 8 quotes "a wild donkey of a man.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Card 2 already asked about the second half of Genesis 16:2 (Sarai's plan to go to Hagar). Card 3 then steps back to the first half of the same verse (her reason) and repeats that Abram listened. The card moves the baker backward instead of forward. Tell the reason before the plan is asked, or fold it into the setup.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: "Plan worked, everybody's happy, roll the credits... oh, friend, HOLD that thought" signals that trouble is coming. That rules out both positive wrong answers on card 6 ("serve her closely" and "thank her daily"), so the baker can pick "despise her" without knowing the text.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer ("She begins to despise her") is the only negative option. Both wrong answers are warm and positive, so the right answer stands out by tone.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: "Sarai is fed up with the contempt" states Sarai's feeling as fact. Genesis 16:5 gives her words, not her feeling.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: This story card is 3 sentences. It isn't the walkthrough's opening card, so only 1 to 2 sentences are allowed.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card tells that Hagar fled from Sarai, which is Genesis 16:6, but it cites only Genesis 16:7.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "Hagar has fled from Sarai" gives away the answer to card 2, where the right answer is "She's running away from Sarai." Stop 1 card 10 only established that Hagar didn't stay put. It never said she fled from Sarai.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke. It tells no part of the passage and doesn't move the baker forward, since Genesis 16:8 was already covered on card 2.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: "His hand will be against everyone, and everyone's hand against him" makes the true or false on card 9 ("live in peace with all his brothers") obviously false. The setup gives away the answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "Eighty-six and a brand-new DAD" is a joke built on Abram's age.

rule.text: Never puts down any person or group: no jokes about age, gender, race, nationality, accents, appearance, intelligence or church denomination.
